title: Regenerative ECLSS subsystem performance, closure and crew-scaling audit for OTA-TEC-0093
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0093 Life-Support core-module dossier. Assess the component-level evidence needed before this proposed reusable component can become active: (1) official/primary performance evidence for regenerative oxygen generation by water electrolysis, CO2 removal/regeneration, Sabatier water recovery, humidity/temperature control and trace-contaminant control; (2) realistic material-closure limits, make-up water/oxygen or other consumables, maintenance, sorbent/catalyst life, pumps/valves/sensors and replacement burden; (3) metabolic loading and crew-size scaling, including why independently valid subsystem values cannot simply be summed into a jointly realistic integrated ECLSS for 6, 20 or 200 people; (4) energy, mass, volume and heat-rejection trade-offs relevant to short-duration rover, multi-day transit and long-duration station variants; (5) fault tolerance, graceful degradation, emergency reserves and what evidence would be needed before phrases such as 'triple redundant life support' could describe a real architecture; (6) whether CYGNUS, PELICAN, lunar rover, Gateway and the early combined vehicle can plausibly share a common core/technology family versus requiring materially different hardware variants; and (7) which `CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_OF` relations could become technically supported without claiming identical hardware. Reuse existing object-level audits where relevant, especially CYGNUS crew-environment research; do not duplicate their questions. Do NOT set NOXIA consumption rates, maintenance costs, crew capacities, unlocks, efficiency bonuses or other balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0093 is an uncovered mapped component and explicitly a test case for the emerging OTA component schema. It centralizes a function repeatedly referenced by several NOXIA vehicles/stations, so resolving its real subsystem limits and variant logic has unusually high cross-project reuse and should precede hardening duplicate life-support assumptions elsewhere.
real_world_anchor: NASA/agency regenerative ECLSS systems and performance data: oxygen generation, CO2 removal, Sabatier recovery, humidity/trace-gas control, water interfaces, crew metabolic loads, reliability and maintenance.
novelty_reason: First exact-source component-level ECLSS synthesis across several OTA technical objects. It tests shared-core versus variant relationships instead of treating repeated 'life support' prose as identical hardware.
